match.reason: The bank point teaches objective and subjective measures of liveability in geography, not how objective and subjective language is used in reports and reviews, so it is related but not the same idea at this depth.

draft.title: Objective and subjective language
card: language sticks to facts that can be checked. It avoids feelings and opinions, so two readers should agree on what it says.
language shows the writer's feelings and opinions. Words such as awful, lovely, boring and best are signs of it.
A news report or science report mostly uses objective language, because its purpose is to inform. A review mostly uses subjective language, because its purpose is to give a judgement.
A review can still contain facts, such as the length of a film. A report can still slip in opinion words. Look at each sentence and ask if it could be checked.
draft.remember: Objective language can be checked. Subjective language shows what the writer thinks or feels.

opts: The school fair raised $2400 for new library books
The school fair was a wonderful day for everyone
The school fair had the tastiest food of the year
The school fair was far too noisy for a library cause
a.why: The amount raised is a fact that could be checked against the records. Wonderful, tastiest and far too noisy are opinions, so they are subjective.
a.clue: Which sentence has no opinion words and could be checked?

b.q: Ava writes a review of a new skate park in Bathurst. Which sentence from her review is objective?
opts: The park has two bowls and a rail that is 12 metres long
The bowls are the most thrilling part of the whole park
The park is a brilliant place to spend a weekend
The rail is too slippery, which makes it dull to ride
b.why: The number of bowls and the length of the rail are facts that someone could measure or count. The other options give opinions, even though they sit in a review, which mostly uses subjective language.
b.clue: A review can still hold a sentence that could be checked.

a.best: The school fair raised $2400 for new library books

b.best: The park has two bowls and a rail that is 12 metres long
